page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for high-throughput graphics, machine learning inference, and parallel computing workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.2 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 384 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 4 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 38 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. Notably, this machine features an accelerator array of eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace generation, supplying an aggregate pool of 192 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. No local storage is included with the instance, requiring all durable and scratch volumes to be attached as networked block storage.

Benchmark outcomes show that the primary performance strengths of the g2-standard-96 lie in GPU-accelerated computing and distributed multi-core processing. LLM inference results place the instance in the top 10% tier for prompt processing across small, medium, and large model architectures, reaching 11,350 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 294 tokens per second on 70B parameter models. Multi-core compute capabilities are reflected in a strong top-25% stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 75,745.7 alongside 63.66 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1072.0) and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25% percentile, reflecting the lower base clock frequency of 2.2 GHz per core.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the g2-standard-96 optimizes resource density by pairing eight energy-efficient enterprise GPUs with high multi-core compute and substantial memory capacity. Tradeoffs include modest single-thread CPU performance and the absence of ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning I/O-intensive pipelines must manage networked storage latencies. The instance profile is primarily aligned with multi-GPU AI/ML inference pipelines, large language model deployment, batch video processing, rendering farms, and highly parallel scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is an accelerator-focused instance offering eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs with 192 GB of total VRAM, powered by 96 vCPUs on 48 physical Intel Xeon cores and 384 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 instructions, it excludes bundled local storage in favor of attached network block volumes. Hardware benchmarks reveal exceptional multi-core throughput and top-tier GPU performance, reaching the top 10% for LLM inference prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as strong multi-core stress testing scores. However, single-core processing metrics, such as Geekbench single-thread and decompression tasks, score in the bottom quartile due to its 2.2 GHz clock speed. With massive parallel execution and high GPU density, g2-standard-96 is suited for multi-GPU model serving, large-scale inference workloads, distributed rendering, and parallelized scientific computing.
